lines.text: My father didn't hesitate. He gave three orders, in the voice he used to call the levy.
Bar the gate. Saddle six horses at the north postern. And bring me my sword.
Come with us, Father. They're coming for you because of me.
They're coming for me because of me. For seventeen years I've done everything quietly, Lucan. Today I'd like to be loud.
Then I'll stand with you.
No. You're my heir. When they take me, someone has to hold the Senn. And someone has to be clever enough to bow.
Maric looked at me. For once in our lives, we wanted the same thing. Neither of us could have it.
The column came up the Senn road at noon. Two hundred royal soldiers in crimson, with twelve Hounds riding in front.
Lord Varr! By the King's warrant, open your gate and surrender the traitor Lucan Varr, or be named a traitor yourself!
I am Lord of Varr, Herald. This is my gate. If the King wants it open, he can come and knock.
Then my father did something I'd only heard of in songs. He laid his hand on the gate, and the gate turned to ice.
Frost ran from his palm across the oak, across the stones, across the whole south wall, hard as iron.
Rime. Five rings, and every one his own. How old-fashioned. Bring up the ram.
We rode out of the north postern while the ram was still breaking itself on my father's ice.
Go on, little brother. It'll build character.
He was smiling when he said it. He was also crying. I didn't mention either.
From the first hill, I looked back. The ice held until sunset. Then the gate came open.
My father walked out alone, and laid his sword down in the road. He didn't look toward the hill. He knew I'd be watching.
They put him in Order chains of glass, to keep his frost in. He held out his wrists like a man accepting a gift.
Where is the boy, my lord?
Gone, Brother. Half a day ago. You'll have to make do with me.
Wren had to hold my horse's bridle to stop me riding back down. Oswin held the other side.
Behind us, Maric's thread burned steady all the way to the river. He stayed. He bowed. He was clever enough.
My father went south in chains. I went north with a price on my head. We had both done exactly what he wanted.
Three days later, on the edge of Penhallow's country, a one-eyed man stepped out of the trees with a bow, and called my name.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and fifteen, coming soon.
